info.title: AFF Payments API
info.description: The Stripe webhook endpoint (cross-cutting: one-off order payments, F1 subscription billing, D4 refunds). Reflects backend/src/modules/payments/payments.controller.ts::handleStripeWebhook and payments.service.ts::processWebhookEvent as implemented. No auth beyond Stripe's own signature header — this file documents event routing, not a typical request/response contract, since the request body is Stripe's own event payload. POST /orders/:id/checkout-session and POST /subscriptions/checkout-session (the endpoints that start the flows this webhook completes) are documented in docs/openapi/orders_openapi.json and docs/openapi/subscriptions_openapi.json respectively.

tags.name: Payments
tags.description: Stripe webhook — the single endpoint that completes order payments, subscription billing, and refunds

post.summary: Stripe webhook — routes one event to its effect based on event.type
post.description: Auth: none (the Stripe-Signature request header, verified against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, replaces JWT auth on this route). The raw, unparsed request body is required for signature verification (see req.rawBody in app.ts) — this is the one route in the API that is not JSON-parsed generically before reaching its handler. Always responds 200 once an event is durably processed or recognized as a duplicate, so Stripe does not retry it; a bad/missing signature is the only rejection.

requestBody.description: A raw Stripe Event payload (docs.stripe.com/api/events/object). Shape varies by event.type — see the event/effect table below.

parameters.name: Stripe-Signature
parameters.description: HMAC signature Stripe computes over the raw request body, verified with STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET

200.description: The event was routed (including a recognized-duplicate or an intentionally no-op event type). See the event/effect table below for what each event.type actually does.

x-event-effect-table.description: Not a formal OpenAPI construct — documents what payments.service.ts#processWebhookEvent does for each event.type, since a single endpoint fans out by payload shape rather than by path/method. Mirrors docs/api_design.md §8; keep both in sync.

events.effect: Look up ORDER via session metadata → ORDER.paymentStatus=PAID, orderStatus=PREPARING; PAYMENT.status=PAID, paidAt=now, stripePaymentIntentId=session.payment_intent; DeliveryService.createForOrder; emit payment:success (docs/api_design.md §12).

No-op (logged only). Nothing is created here — there's no invoice/period data on the Checkout Session itself. The SUBSCRIPTION row is appended by invoice.paid below, which fires immediately after for both the first payment and every renewal.

Append a new SUBSCRIPTION row for the new billing cycle (append-only ledger, docs/database_design.md): status=ACTIVE, currentPeriodEnd converted from invoice.lines.data[0].period.end (falling back to invoice.period_end), stripeInvoiceId=invoice.id. Then send the Premium confirmation email (Nodemailer) — only when the row is newly created.
events.idempotency: Guards on SUBSCRIPTION.stripeInvoiceId (unique, sparse) — a re-delivered event finds the existing row by invoice id and appends nothing a second time, so no duplicate email either.

events.effect: Latest SUBSCRIPTION.status=PAST_DUE for the Recipient resolved from invoice.customer. GET /subscriptions/me then derives tier=STANDARD.
Reconcile cancelAtPeriodEnd on the latest SUBSCRIPTION row from event.data.object.cancel_at_period_end. Optional — PATCH /subscriptions/me's response is the primary source of truth for the flag.

Latest SUBSCRIPTION.status=CANCELLED for the Recipient resolved from event.data.object.customer. Fires at currentPeriodEnd for a cancel_at_period_end cancellation started via PATCH /subscriptions/me (docs/openapi/subscriptions_openapi.json). GET /subscriptions/me then derives tier=STANDARD.

Confirms a refund initiated by DELETE /orders/:id (docs/openapi/orders_openapi.json) actually settled. Ignored unless event.data.object.status=succeeded. Look up PAYMENT via stripeRefundId=event.data.object.id → PAYMENT.status=REFUNDED, refundedAt=now; ORDER.paymentStatus=REFUNDED; emit payment:refunded (docs/api_design.md §12). No matching PAYMENT (e.g. stripeRefundId not yet persisted) is safe to ignore. Used instead of the older charge.refunded event, which as of Stripe's 2024-10-28 API change no longer reliably carries refund id/status in its payload.
Ignored — not part of the documented flow. The controller still responds 200 so Stripe doesn't retry it.

data.description: Always null — this endpoint's response body carries no information back to Stripe

InvalidSignature.description: The Stripe-Signature header is missing, or does not verify against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET for the given raw body

value.message: Missing Stripe-Signature header or request body.
No signatures found matching the expected signature for payload
